```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE)
r <- readRDS(params$results_rds)
if (inherits(r, "PopgenVCFAnalysis")) {
  a <- r
  r <- c(
    list(
      metadata = a$samples$metadata,
      qc_snps = a$variants$qc_ids,
      final_snps = a$variants$ld_ids,
      qc = a$variants$reports,
      package_version = a$package_version,
      messages = a$messages
    ),
    a$results
  )
}
report_figures <- params$figures
html_escape <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("&", "&amp;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("<", "&lt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub(">", "&gt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub('"', "&quot;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x
}
# kable(..., longtable = TRUE) alone does not repeat its header on later
# pages (that needs \endfirsthead/\endhead, which base knitr's longtable
# support doesn't add) -- inserted here by hand at the one \midrule that
# always immediately follows the single header row kable() emits, valid
# minimal longtable syntax (everything above \endhead repeats as the page
# header; omitting \endfirsthead just reuses it for the first page too).
report_kable_repeat_header <- function(rendered) {
  lines <- strsplit(rendered, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
  idx <- which(lines == "\\midrule")[1L]
  if (is.na(idx)) return(rendered)
  paste(append(lines, "\\endhead", after = idx), collapse = "\n")
}

# A long free-text column (e.g. a pipeline-notice message) forced every
# other column in the same row down to an illegibly tiny \resizebox scale on
# a real production report -- confirmed directly. LaTeX tabular/longtable
# cells never wrap on their own; kable() has already produced correctly
# escaped, correctly rounded cell text by this point, so this only performs
# a surgical column-position substitution on kable()'s own trusted data-row
# lines (between the \endhead inserted above and \bottomrule), wrapping each
# long column's already-escaped content in \parbox rather than
# re-implementing kable's formatting.
report_kable_wrap_long_columns <- function(rendered, table, threshold = 40L, width_frac = 0.55) {
  wrap_idx <- which(vapply(seq_along(table), function(i) {
    col <- table[[i]]
    (is.character(col) || is.factor(col)) &&
      any(nchar(as.character(col)) > threshold, na.rm = TRUE)
  }, logical(1L)))
  if (!length(wrap_idx)) return(rendered)
  lines <- strsplit(rendered, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
  head_end <- which(lines == "\\endhead")[1L]
  foot_start <- which(lines == "\\bottomrule")[1L]
  if (is.na(head_end) || is.na(foot_start) || head_end >= foot_start - 1L) return(rendered)
  width_expr <- sprintf("%.2f\\textwidth", width_frac / length(wrap_idx))
  ncol <- length(table)
  for (i in seq(head_end + 1L, foot_start - 1L)) {
    line <- lines[[i]]
    if (!grepl("\\\\\\\\[ \t]*$", line)) next
    body <- sub("\\\\\\\\[ \t]*$", "", line)
    cells <- strsplit(body, " & ", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
    if (length(cells) != ncol) next
    for (j in wrap_idx) cells[[j]] <- sprintf("\\parbox[t]{%s}{%s}", width_expr, cells[[j]])
    lines[[i]] <- paste0(paste(cells, collapse = " & "), "\\\\")
  }
  paste(lines, collapse = "\n")
}

# \resizebox can perfectly, continuously scale a table down to exactly fit
# \textwidth -- but it can't wrap a longtable at all (resizebox measures one
# finished box; a longtable's whole point is breaking across an unknown
# number of pages, which can't be pre-measured as one box). Confirmed
# directly: a discrete font-size fallback alone (no resizebox) still let
# very wide tables (a real DAPC/PCA-scores-shaped 10-32 numeric-column
# table) overflow \textwidth even at \scriptsize, a real regression against
# the original \resizebox behaviour for exactly the common case (a table
# that fits on one page but has many columns) that behaviour was written
# for. So the choice is made per table, by \sbox-measuring a throwaway
# plain-tabular copy of the exact same (already wrapped) cell content: a
# table whose natural height already exceeds most of a page cannot use
# \resizebox regardless (it needs to paginate) and gets longtable with the
# coarser discrete-size fallback; everything else -- the large majority of
# real result tables -- keeps the original, exact-fit \resizebox behaviour,
# completely unchanged from before longtable existed here.
report_kable_render <- function(longtable_body) {
  lines <- strsplit(longtable_body, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
  tabular_lines <- lines[lines != "\\endhead"]
  # Located by content, not a fixed index -- kable()'s own output carries a
  # leading blank line before \begin{longtable}, which a fixed-position
  # substitution silently missed (confirmed directly: produced a
  # \begin{longtable}...\end{tabular} mismatch, a hard LaTeX compile error).
  begin_idx <- grep("^\\\\begin\\{longtable\\}", tabular_lines)[1L]
  end_idx <- grep("^\\\\end\\{longtable\\}$", tabular_lines)[1L]
  if (!is.na(begin_idx)) {
    tabular_lines[begin_idx] <- sub("^\\\\begin\\{longtable\\}", "\\\\begin{tabular}", tabular_lines[begin_idx])
  }
  if (!is.na(end_idx)) {
    tabular_lines[end_idx] <- sub("^\\\\end\\{longtable\\}$", "\\\\end{tabular}", tabular_lines[end_idx])
  }
  tabular_body <- paste(tabular_lines, collapse = "\n")
  # A raw-LaTeX line whose very first character is a bare "{" or "}" (not
  # attached to a preceding backslash command) is not recognized by
  # pandoc's raw-tex passthrough inside a results='asis' chunk -- confirmed
  # directly: it rendered as a literal, visible brace character in the
  # compiled PDF instead of functioning as TeX grouping. \begingroup/
  # \endgroup (both backslash commands, like every other line here) give
  # the same scoping without ever starting a line with a bare brace.
  paste0(
    "\\sbox{\\pgvcftablebox}{\\begingroup\n", tabular_body, "\n\\endgroup}\n",
    # \ht alone is only the box's height above its own reference point, not
    # its full visual extent -- confirmed directly on a real 80-row table,
    # \ht came in just under the threshold (531pt vs. a 533pt cutoff) while
    # \ht+\dp (1058pt) was unambiguously over it, sending an 80-row table
    # down the non-paginating \resizebox branch instead and silently
    # dropping every row past where it overflowed the page, the exact
    # defect this whole function exists to prevent. Every real caller of
    # this box (pandoc's own image-scaling macro included) uses \ht+\dp for
    # the same reason.
    "\\ifdim\\dimexpr\\ht\\pgvcftablebox+\\dp\\pgvcftablebox\\relax>0.82\\textheight\n",
    "\\ifdim\\wd\\pgvcftablebox>1.5\\textwidth\n\\def\\pgvcftablesize{\\scriptsize}\n",
    "\\else\\ifdim\\wd\\pgvcftablebox>1.15\\textwidth\n\\def\\pgvcftablesize{\\footnotesize}\n",
    "\\else\\ifdim\\wd\\pgvcftablebox>\\textwidth\n\\def\\pgvcftablesize{\\small}\n",
    "\\else\n\\def\\pgvcftablesize{\\normalsize}\n",
    "\\fi\\fi\\fi\n",
    "\\begingroup\\pgvcftablesize\n", longtable_body, "\n\\endgroup\n",
    "\\else\n",
    "\\ifdim\\wd\\pgvcftablebox>\\textwidth\n",
    "\\resizebox{\\textwidth}{!}{\\begingroup\n", tabular_body, "\n\\endgroup}\n",
    "\\else\n",
    "\\begingroup\n", tabular_body, "\n\\endgroup\n",
    "\\fi\n",
    "\\fi\n"
  )
}

report_kable <- function(table, digits = NULL) {
  # kable()'s default ("pipe") output is pandoc markdown, meant to be
  # converted by pandoc's own markdown-to-LaTeX pass -- fine standalone, but
  # NOT valid content inside raw LaTeX (which pandoc never re-processes for
  # embedded markdown table syntax). LaTeX output explicitly requests
  # format="latex" so kable() itself emits real longtable source, safe to
  # measure/wrap directly. longtable (not a plain, page-bound tabular) is
  # required so a table taller than one page paginates instead of silently
  # overflowing past the physical page and losing rows -- confirmed
  # directly on a real production report (a >100-row table's tail simply
  # never appeared anywhere in the rendered PDF).
  latex <- knitr::is_latex_output()
  args <- list(x = table, format = if (latex) "latex" else "pipe")
  if (!is.null(digits)) args$digits <- digits
  if (latex) args <- c(args, list(booktabs = TRUE, longtable = TRUE))
  rendered <- do.call(knitr::kable, args)
  if (!latex) {
    cat(rendered, sep = "\n")
    cat("\n\n")
    return(invisible(TRUE))
  }
  rendered <- report_kable_repeat_header(rendered)
  rendered <- report_kable_wrap_long_columns(rendered, table)
  cat(report_kable_render(rendered))
  cat("\n")
  invisible(TRUE)
}

report_table_section <- function(title, table, digits = NULL, level = 1L) {
  # A genuinely zero-column table (write_chromosome_results() returns a bare
  # data.table() when no chromosome met chromosome_min_snps) is not NULL,
  # but knitr::kable(format="latex") on it emits \begin{tabular}{} -- an
  # empty column spec that is invalid LaTeX and hard-crashes the PDF
  # compile. length() on a data.frame/data.table is its column count.
  if (is.null(table) || !length(table)) return(invisible(FALSE))
  cat(strrep("#", level), " ", title, "\n\n", sep = "")
  report_kable(table, digits)
  invisible(TRUE)
}
```

# Executive summary

This `r toupper(params$report_format)` file is a portable, human-readable
analysis report. Figures are embedded directly in the file. The HTML version
can be opened in a standard web browser, while the PDF version is optimized for
compact exchange, printing, and email. The accompanying `analysis_results.rds`
file is a reproducibility archive for
R users; it is not required to read this report.

`r if (!is.null(r$package_version)) sprintf("Generated with **popgenVCF v%s**.", r$package_version)`

The analysis retained **`r nrow(r$metadata)` samples** from **`r data.table::uniqueN(r$metadata$population)` populations**, with **`r length(r$qc_snps)` QC-passing SNPs** and **`r length(r$final_snps)` LD-pruned SNPs**.

```{r analysis-sections, results='asis'}
pipeline_notices <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$messages) && nrow(r$messages)) {
  pipeline_notices <- r$messages[r$messages$level %in% c("WARNING", "INFO"), c("stage", "level", "message")]
  if (!nrow(pipeline_notices)) pipeline_notices <- NULL
}
report_table_section("Pipeline notices", pipeline_notices)
if (!is.null(r$fst$global) && length(r$fst$global) &&
    is.finite(r$fst$global[[1L]])) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "The global Weir-Cockerham $F_{ST}$ estimate was **%.4f**.\n\n",
    r$fst$global[[1L]]
  ))
}
report_table_section("Quality control", r$qc$sequential, digits = 2)
report_table_section("Genetic diversity", r$diversity$population, digits = 4)
private_alleles <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$diversity$locus)) {
  pa <- r$diversity$locus[
    !is.na(r$diversity$locus$private_allele) & r$diversity$locus$private_allele != "none",
    c("population", "snp_id", "chromosome", "position", "private_allele",
      "alternate_allele_count", "reference_allele_count")
  ]
  if (nrow(pa)) private_alleles <- head(pa, 20)
}
report_table_section("Private alleles (up to 20 shown; see 32_private_alleles.tsv for the complete list)", private_alleles)
report_table_section(
  "Principal component analysis",
  if (!is.null(r$pca$scores)) head(r$pca$scores, 20) else NULL,
  digits = 4
)
pca_loadings_top <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$pca$loadings) && nrow(r$pca$loadings)) {
  pca_loadings_top <- head(r$pca$loadings[order(-r$pca$loadings$magnitude), ], 20)
}
report_table_section(
  "PCA SNP loadings (top 20 by |loading|; see 31_PCA_loadings.tsv for the complete top-N list)",
  pca_loadings_top, digits = 4
)
report_table_section("Population differentiation", r$fst$long, digits = 4)
population_distance_table <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$population_tree$distance) && nrow(r$population_tree$distance)) {
  population_distance_table <- as.data.frame(r$population_tree$distance)
  population_distance_table <- cbind(population = rownames(population_distance_table), population_distance_table)
  rownames(population_distance_table) <- NULL
}
report_table_section(
  "Nei's standard genetic distance between populations (see 46_population_genetic_distance.tsv; a neighbour-joining tree with bootstrap support at each node, alongside the individual-level IBS tree, is written and rendered as a figure when at least three populations are present -- see 52_IBS_tree and 53_population_tree)",
  population_distance_table, digits = 4
)
report_table_section(
  "Genome scan FST outliers (top 20 windows by FST; see 39_genome_scan_fst.tsv for the complete list)",
  r$genome_scan$outliers, digits = 4
)
pcadapt_top <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$pcadapt$table)) {
  sig <- r$pcadapt$table[!is.na(r$pcadapt$table$q_value) & r$pcadapt$table$q_value < 0.05, ]
  if (nrow(sig)) pcadapt_top <- head(sig[order(sig$q_value), ], 20)
}
report_table_section(
  "pcadapt outlier scan (top 20 significant loci by q-value; see 59_pcadapt_outliers.tsv for the complete results and 59b_pcadapt_significant_outliers.tsv for the complete significant list)",
  pcadapt_top, digits = 4
)
report_table_section(
  "Linkage disequilibrium decay (mean r-squared by physical distance bin; see 43_LD_decay.tsv for the complete list)",
  r$ld_decay$binned, digits = 4
)
report_table_section(
  "LD-based effective population size (per population; see 45_Ne_LD.tsv for full diagnostics)",
  r$ne_ld, digits = 4
)
close_relatives <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$kinship$close_relatives) && nrow(r$kinship$close_relatives)) {
  close_relatives <- head(r$kinship$close_relatives, 20)
}
report_table_section(
  "Close relatives (up to 20 shown; see 36_close_relatives.tsv for the complete list)",
  close_relatives, digits = 4
)
sex_check_top <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$sex_check$table) && nrow(r$sex_check$table)) {
  sc <- r$sex_check$table
  if ("status" %in% names(sc) && any(!is.na(sc$status))) {
    priority <- match(sc$status, c("discordant", "mismatch", "ambiguous", "not_reported", "match"))
    priority[is.na(priority)] <- 5L
    sc <- sc[order(priority, sc$x_heterozygosity_F), ]
  } else {
    sc <- sc[order(sc$x_heterozygosity_F), ]
  }
  sex_check_top <- head(sc, 20)
}
report_table_section(
  "Sex check (reported vs inferred sex from X-chromosome heterozygosity and Y-chromosome call rate; up to 20 shown, discordant and ambiguous calls first; see 42_sex_check.tsv for the complete list)",
  sex_check_top, digits = 4
)
roh_top <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$roh$sample_summary) && nrow(r$roh$sample_summary)) {
  roh_top <- head(r$roh$sample_summary[order(-r$roh$sample_summary$froh), ], 20)
}
report_table_section(
  "Runs of homozygosity (highest FROH samples, up to 20 shown; see 38_ROH_sample_summary.tsv for the complete list)",
  roh_top, digits = 4
)
report_table_section(
  "Discriminant analysis of principal components",
  r$dapc$diagnostics,
  digits = 4
)
dapc_loadings_top <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$dapc$models) && length(r$dapc$models)) {
  loading_tables <- lapply(names(r$dapc$models), function(k) {
    loadings <- r$dapc$models[[k]]$loadings
    if (is.null(loadings) || !nrow(loadings)) return(NULL)
    cbind(K = k, loadings[, c("axis", "snp_id", "chromosome", "position", "contribution")])
  })
  loading_tables <- loading_tables[!vapply(loading_tables, is.null, logical(1L))]
  if (length(loading_tables)) {
    combined <- do.call(rbind, loading_tables)
    dapc_loadings_top <- head(combined[order(-combined$contribution), ], 20)
  }
}
report_table_section(
  "DAPC SNP loadings (top 20 by contribution across all K; see 22f_DAPC_loadings_K<k>.tsv for the complete per-K top-N lists)",
  dapc_loadings_top, digits = 4
)
if (!is.null(r$amova)) {
  cat("# Analysis of molecular variance\n\n")
  if (!is.null(r$amova$components)) {
    report_kable(r$amova$components, digits = 4)
  }
  if (!is.null(r$amova$phi)) {
    report_kable(r$amova$phi, digits = 4)
  }
}
report_table_section(
  "Multilocus genotype (MLG) and clonal diversity",
  r$clonality$summary, digits = 4
)
clonality_groups <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$clonality$groups) && nrow(r$clonality$groups)) {
  clonality_groups <- head(r$clonality$groups, 20)
}
report_table_section(
  "Samples sharing an identical multilocus genotype (up to 20 groups shown; see 57_MLG_groups.tsv for the complete list)",
  clonality_groups
)
if (!is.null(r$sexbias)) {
  cat("# Sex-biased dispersal test\n\n")
  cat(sprintf(
    "%s test: statistic = %.3f, p = %.4f (n = %d female, %d male%s). See 60_sexbias_AIc_by_sample.tsv for per-sample assignment indices.\n\n",
    r$sexbias$test, r$sexbias$statistic, r$sexbias$p_value,
    r$sexbias$n_female, r$sexbias$n_male,
    if (r$sexbias$permutations > 0) sprintf(", %d permutations", r$sexbias$permutations) else ""
  ))
}
report_table_section(
  "Mantel test and isolation by distance", r$ibd$summary, digits = 4
)
report_table_section(
  "Admixture-model cross-validation", r$admixture_cv, digits = 6
)
report_table_section(
  "Chromosome-specific results", r$chromosome_summary, digits = 4
)
```

# Figure gallery

The gallery contains one version of every analysis figure. The HTML report
prefers browser-friendly SVG or PNG files. The PDF report prefers the compact
vector PDF source for each figure. Original files remain available in the
sibling `figures/` directory.

```{r figure-gallery, results='asis'}
if (is.null(report_figures) || !nrow(report_figures)) {
  cat("No figure files were found. Configure `output.figure_formats` to include `pdf`, `png`, or `svg`, then regenerate the report.\n")
} else if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(report_figures))) {
    figure <- report_figures[i, , drop = FALSE]
    caption <- html_escape(figure$caption[[1L]])
    filename <- html_escape(basename(figure$path[[1L]]))
    uri <- knitr::image_uri(figure$path[[1L]])
    if (identical(figure$format[[1L]], "pdf")) {
      cat(sprintf(
        paste0(
          '<figure style="margin:2em 0">',
          '<figcaption><strong>%s</strong><br><small>%s</small></figcaption>',
          '<p><a href="%s" target="_blank">Open the embedded PDF figure</a></p>',
          '</figure>\n'
        ),
        caption, filename, uri
      ))
    } else {
      cat(sprintf(
        paste0(
          '<figure style="margin:2em 0">',
          '<img src="%s" alt="%s" loading="lazy" ',
          'style="display:block;max-width:100%%;height:auto;margin:auto">',
          '<figcaption style="text-align:center;margin-top:0.5em">',
          '<strong>%s</strong><br><small>%s</small></figcaption>',
          '</figure>\n'
        ),
        uri, caption, caption, filename
      ))
    }
  }
} else {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(report_figures))) {
    figure <- report_figures[i, , drop = FALSE]
    caption <- figure$caption[[1L]]
    path <- gsub(" ", "%20", figure$path[[1L]], fixed = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf(
      "![%s](%s){width=95%%}\n\n\\newpage\n\n",
      caption, path
    ))
  }
}
```

# Reproducibility

This report was generated from the serialized pipeline result object. Exact input hashes, settings, package versions, and stage runtimes are stored alongside the report.

```{r reproducibility-sections, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(r$dapc) && "replicate_max_rmse" %in% names(r$dapc$diagnostics)) {
  report_table_section(
    "Population-structure reproducibility",
    r$dapc$diagnostics[, c("K", "assignment_accuracy", "replicate_max_rmse")],
    digits = 4, level = 2L
  )
}
if (!is.null(r$faststructure$runs)) {
  report_table_section("fastStructure", r$faststructure$runs, level = 2L)
}
if (!is.null(r$snmf$diagnostics)) {
  report_table_section(
    "Sparse non-negative matrix factorization",
    r$snmf$diagnostics,
    digits = 6, level = 2L
  )
}
```
